svg.text: Why 224 loads become 40: one 16 × 16 piece at a time
Every operand of the two multiplies is read from shared memory in 16 × 16 pieces of bf16. Each of the warp's 32 lanes must end up
holding 8 values of the piece, as 4 pairs packed into 4 registers (2 values per 32-bit register). Counts are instructions per warp.
v1, a piece of Q, K or P: one plain load per pair
The 4 pairs a lane needs sit in 4 different places, one in each 8 × 8 tile. Each pair
is two neighbours in memory, so one 32-bit load (LDS) can fetch it. But an LDS
fetches one address per lane, so a lane needs 4 of them:

svg.text: = 4 instructions per piece. All 32 lanes run them together, each at its own addresses.
v1, a piece of V: worse, because its pairs are not neighbours
O = P·V wants each pair to be 2 keys of the same head dim. V is stored one key per
row, so the two values of a pair are a whole row (128 bytes) apart. Each needs its
own 16-bit load, then a PRMT instruction packs the two halves into one register:

svg.text: v2: one ldmatrix per piece, for every operand
lanes that give each tile's 8 row addresses
ldmatrix.x4 is one instruction for the whole warp. Each of the 32 lanes gives the address
of one 8-value row (8 rows × 4 tiles = 32 rows). The hardware reads all 4 tiles and
deals every lane its 4 pairs, already packed in 4 registers.

svg.text: V, rows and columns swapped on the way (.trans), so the

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: pairs come out as 2 keys of one dim: replaces 8 LDS.U16 + 4 PRMT
Add it up over one pass of the loop (one key block)
Each warp multiplies its own 16 rows of Q by the whole 64 × 64 tile of K, then its 16 rows of P by the whole tile of V. So it reads:
All the instructions in one pass of the loop
288 load-and-pack instructions become 40: 248 fewer. Everything else is the same work in both (the 64 multiplies, the softmax,
the copies of the next K and V) and differs only by 4 address instructions, 306 → 302. Together: 594 → 342.
Every shared-memory instruction goes through the load/store pipe. With 248 fewer per pass, it falls from 72.5% to 26.0% busy,
stops holding up the multiplies, and the tensor cores rise from 71.3% to 86.9% of peak.
